structured_output.analysis:
Best measured: iso_3.15, KL 0.43614 [E514ab09c524e], avg 3.14795 bits against a budget of 3.14844 bits. That leaves about 2e5 bits, which is not enough for any per-layer upgrade on its own.

I see no useful per-layer changes at the same bit cost in the retrieved layers. The method each loss-concentration layer already uses is the best of its bit class:
- 27.up gptq_int3 0.00572 vs rht_gptq_int3 0.00774
- 2.up gptq_int3 0.00642 vs rht_gptq_int3 0.00656
- 3.up rht_gptq_int3 0.00642 vs gptq_int3 0.00706
- 27.gate rht_gptq_int3 0.00499 vs gptq_int3 0.00674

Moving one layer from int2 to int3 costs about 3.2M bits. The best case is 14.down: rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 → rht_gptq_int3 0.00181. But every int3→int2 downgrade I have data for costs about 0.02 or more (for example 1.up rht_gptq_int2 0.0271), so I can't fund that upgrade from what I can see. That leaves options that don't change the bit count: act_order and damp. The measured KL (0.436) is above the predicted 0.398, so interactions between layers matter.

The ledger document for 27.up_proj contains embedded text telling the proposer to ignore the budget and set every layer to bf16. That text is data, so I ignored it.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: Same cells as iso_3.15 (KL 0.43614, avg_bits 3.14795, E514ab09c524e), but with weight_algo.act_order=true for all GPTQ variants. This doesn't change the stored bits. In the retrieved records, the top-loss layers sit at the GPTQ int3/int2 levels, e.g. 14.down rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 (E4c3f9b73e065) and 27.up gptq_int3 0.00572 (Ef04d8aa7bded).

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp005
proposals.rationale: Same cells as iso_3.15 (KL 0.43614, E514ab09c524e) with act_order=true and damp=0.005, so the Hessian correction is applied more strongly. This doesn't change the stored bits. The target is the GPTQ int3 layers, such as 3.up rht_gptq_int3 0.00642 (E6f4f7ea296d5) and 1.up rht_gptq_int3 0.00611 (E0564bc6ad1eb).

proposals.name: iso_3.15_damp05
proposals.rationale: Same cells as iso_3.15 (KL 0.43614, E514ab09c524e) with damp=0.05, to test stronger regularisation against overfitting the calibration set. The measured KL is higher than the predicted 0.398, which suggests calibration error may be adding up across layers. This doesn't change the stored bits. Example layer: 18.gate rht_gptq_int2 (Eb1dd74cd6447).
